advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that compose_signer/_read_path_source rejects a REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH whose mode has group/other bits set (e.g. 0644).
evidence: src/rebar/opcert_service/keyprov.py:108: `if st.st_mode & 0o077:`
keyprov module docstring lists 'too-permissive' as a rejection case (keyprov.py:40)

tests/unit/test_rp04_s6_opcert_startup_heldout.py enumerates test_compose_rejects_when_no_source_set / both_sources_set / unreadable_key_path / non_ed25519_key / invalid_source (garbage) — no test asserts a 0644/group-readable key file is rejected
ticket 6f14 AC1: 'Exactly-one-source validation rejects every named invalid case ... The path source also needs a 0600-or-stricter regular-file check.'
keyprov.py:108-112: `if st.st_mode & 0o077: raise OpcertKeyError(... 'must be 0600 or stricter'...)`
AC1 in test_rp04_s6_opcert_startup_heldout.py docstring lists 'unreadable / non-Ed25519' but no too-permissive case
search for `0o0` in tests/unit returned (no matches); the heldout AC1 tests (lines 119-161) cover no-source, both-set, unreadable, non-Ed25519, and malformed garbage — none sets a loose mode
advisory.finding: The '0600-or-stricter' file-permission rejection path in _read_path_source (rejecting group/other bits via `st.st_mode & 0o077`) — an explicitly enumerated AC1 rejection case ('too-permissive') — has no covering test, while every sibling rejection case (unreadable, both-set, no-source, non-Ed25519, malformed) does.
merged_from: The too-permissive-mode rejection branch (group/other bits set on the key file) is untested. compose_signer/_read_path_source raises OpcertKeyError when st.st_mode & 0o077, but no test writes a 0644 (or otherwise group/other-readable) key file and asserts rejection. A regression that dropped the permission check would pass the whole suite.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pop/scrub `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY` from `os.environ` immediately after `compose_signer` reads it (and note it bypasses the file-source permission validation).
evidence: config.py:79 `raw = os.environ.get("REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY")` returns the key verbatim; no code path clears the env var after use

keyprov.py `_read_source_key`: the FILE branch calls `_read_path_source(key_path)` which enforces `stat.S_ISREG` + `st.st_mode & 0o077` (0600-or-stricter), but the inline branch is only `return private_key.encode("utf-8")` — no equivalent gating
keyprov.py `_read_path_source` lines 106-112 apply the perms check ONLY to the file source

app.py:171 `app.state.config = OpcertServiceConfig.from_env()` and lifespan compose_signer never pop REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY from os.environ — the secret persists and is inherited by the ssh-keygen/git child processes spawned per job
advisory.finding: The inline-PEM key source `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY` is read into config and used verbatim, but the raw Ed25519 private key remains in `os.environ` for the process lifetime (never unset after compose_signer) — so it is inherited by every child subprocess (ssh-keygen, git, gate LLM ops) and readable via /proc/<pid>/environ. Unlike the FILE source, the inline PEM also bypasses the 0600/regular-file permission validation.
scenarios: A deployment using the REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY compat fallback leaks the op-cert private key to any child process env or /proc/<pid>/environ read
A gate LLM op or git subprocess spawned with inherited environ carries the signing key
advisory.suggested_fix: After compose_signer materializes the process-owned copy, del os.environ['REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY'] (and clear cfg.private_key) so the raw key is not inherited by child processes or readable via /proc/<pid>/environ.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `infra/compose/opcert-ed25519-key` (and `infra/compose/rebar-bot-signing-key` / `*.XXXXXX`) to .gitignore so materialized private keys can never be committed.
evidence: `.gitignore:88:  infra/compose/.env` — only the .env is ignored
search_files `.gitignore` for `opcert-ed25519-key` -> (no matches)
search_files `.gitignore` for `rebar-bot-signing-key` -> (no matches)
fetch-secrets.sh:126 `opcert_key_path="$(dirname "${ENV_FILE}")/opcert-ed25519-key"` writes the key next to .env
docker-compose.yml:290 `- ./opcert-ed25519-key:/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key:ro` mounts that file
advisory.finding: The newly materialized private signing key file infra/compose/opcert-ed25519-key (and its transient mktemp `*.XXXXXX` temp files) is NOT git-ignored; .gitignore only ignores infra/compose/.env, so an Ed25519 PRIVATE op-cert signing key can be accidentally committed to the repo.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `infra/compose/opcert-ed25519-key` and `infra/compose/opcert-ed25519-key.*` (plus the existing rebar-bot key) to .gitignore under the ephemeral-container-secrets block.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Run the opcert service as a dedicated non-root USER in Dockerfile.opcert to reduce blast radius around the mounted private signing key.
evidence: Dockerfile.opcert has no `USER` directive; final instructions are `ENV PATH=...` (line 40), `ENV REBAR_OPCERT_PORT=8080` (42), `EXPOSE 8080` (43), `CMD ["uvicorn", ...]` (46-47)
docker-compose.yml:290 bind-mounts the private key `./opcert-ed25519-key:/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key:ro` into this container
keyprov.py `compose_signer` copies the key into a process-owned 0700 dir and runs ssh-keygen — as the container's (root) user
advisory.finding: Dockerfile.opcert declares no USER, so the op-cert gate service — including the code that copies the private key into a runtime dir and shells `ssh-keygen -Y sign` — runs as root inside the container, mounting a private signing key into a root process (larger blast radius than needed).
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a non-root user (e.g. `RUN useradd -r opcert` and `USER opcert`) before CMD, ensuring the venv and the bind-mounted key are readable by that uid.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a cleanup trap (or ignore pattern) for the mktemp temp key files so an interrupted fetch-secrets.sh does not leave private-key fragments in infra/compose.
evidence: fetch-secrets.sh:127 `opcert_key_tmp="$(mktemp "${opcert_key_path}.XXXXXX")"`
fetch-secrets.sh:129-131 write the key then `mv -f "${opcert_key_tmp}" "${opcert_key_path}"` — a crash before mv leaves the temp file
No cleanup trap covers `opcert_key_tmp`; .gitignore does not cover `*.XXXXXX`
advisory.finding: fetch-secrets.sh materializes the op-cert key via `mktemp "${opcert_key_path}.XXXXXX"` inside infra/compose; an interruption between mktemp and `mv -f` can leave transient 0600 private-key temp files behind in the compose directory, which are also not git-ignored.
advisory.suggested_fix: Register `trap 'rm -f "${opcert_key_tmp}" "${key_tmp}" "${tmp}"' EXIT` (guarded for unset vars) and add `infra/compose/*.XXXXXX` to .gitignore.
